Nord-Kivu (page 7): 509 hospitalized (58 children under five), 3 critical; global CTE/CT occupancy printed 81.0% (332/410), suspects 166/192 (86.5%) and confirmed 166/218 (76.1%); 177 patients (34.8%) in facilities that are not CTE/CT. 332+177=509 reconciles. Tshopo: 13 patients for 36 beds (36.1%); 3 suspect admissions and 2 recovered exits; 4 confirmed cases from Bafwasende lost to follow-up.
Haut-Uele: 29 patients (9 confirmed, 20 suspects) for 169 beds (17.2%); 4 admissions and 28 exits, 7 of them recoveries at Pawa.
Bas-Uele: 47 patients in isolation after 20 admissions and no exit; its 3 beds for confirmed patients are full.
challenges: Contacts 24679/31725 (77.8%), up from 76.9% but below the 95% threshold; 7046 unseen (22.2%). Nord-Kivu is insufficient at 79.7% (15394/19316) and Bunia is critical at 38.8%; Ituri prints no provincial count.

Alerts: all 3184 verified, 556 validated as suspects, 533 investigated (95.9%) and 272 transferred (printed 51.0%, which is over the 533 investigated). The 23 suspects not investigated are 20 in Nord-Kivu and 3 in Ituri; Sud-Ubangi prints ND.

PoE/PoC completeness 106/120 (88.3%): Tshopo 55.6% (10/18) and Sud-Kivu 55.6% (5/9), where the Kavimvira, Kalundu port and Baraka PoE have no isolation set-up; in Nord-Kivu the Butuhe PoC stays closed since the 26 September security incident, alert cells do not handle PoC alerts on time, and insecurity on the Butembo axis, IPC and PPE stock-outs and the lack of a dedicated ambulance persist; Ituri lacks supervision mobility at Rwampara, Nizi and Bunia, September provider pay is late, the Mandima PoCs need an ambulance and the Avakubi PoC is non-functional for insecurity; in Bas-Uele 4 of 20 PoC did not report (Garre Dingila, Mangite, Nawiwi and PK5 Dakwa) and PNHF services, training, provider motivation, water, mobility, connectivity and digitalisation are lacking.

Ituri: 9 of 38 rings unopened, 5 of 39 households not decontaminated, 21 EDS failed and 18 of 104 bodies (17.3%) not swabbed; Nord-Kivu: 13 of 22 rings unopened (notably Katwa and Beni), 7 of 15 households not decontaminated, no household kits (0/8), 44 EDS postponed and one body not swabbed at Vuhovi because of community resistance; Tshopo short of IPC supplies and IPC-trained providers, with water supply problematic and 5 of 6 EDS not done in the absence of families; Bas-Uele no EDS done for 3 alerts, 16 of 20 priority facilities without functional triage, none with mattresses, 17 of 20 without 72-hour water storage and weak community death alert reporting; Haut-Uele 2 families refused EDS and swab in Isiro, only 4 of 7 zones sent IPC reports, and IPC kits and mobility are lacking.

Ituri: low capacity at some CTE/CT (Kilo, Lolwa, Mandima and Biakato), 57 critical patients, blood supply short of needs, no food for 9 patients in Mandima (CT Mandima and CT Makeke) and ambulance movement reporting 17/33.
Nord-Kivu: suspect beds 86.5% occupied (166/192), 177 of 509 hospitalized patients (34.8%) cared for outside CTE/CT, and data completeness 86% (Kyondo and Vuhovi missing).
Tshopo: no food or nutrition support for frontline workers in Bafwasende, and 4 confirmed cases from Bafwasende lost to follow-up.

Bas-Uele: the standard CTE at HGR Buta is delayed, 44 suspects are isolated in health facilities without nutrition support and psychosocial support for its 3 confirmed cases is delayed; Haut-Uele: weak network coverage at some CTE, staff demotivation, short nutritional inputs (F-75, F-100, Plumpy'Nut) and poor water and electricity supply.

Ituri frontline-worker vaccination with Ervebo and the vaccine efficacy research are paused pending research committee validation, and the frontline-worker targets remain to be redefined; Nord-Kivu coverage stays low (6.6% in Beni, against a provincial target of 36070 frontline workers in 15 zones) and ARKTEK transport remains to be confirmed with WHO; Bas-Uele cold-chain units are not running; Tshopo's daily vaccination data could not be used; Haut-Uele's Isiro EPI antenna has had no BCG since 25 September 2026 and its ultra-cold freezers are broken. Vaccine logistics do not establish efficacy against Bundibugyo.

Nord-Kivu: an assessment of CH Kyaghala found 4 of 108 providers trained in IPC and a TB/HIV medicine stock-out. Bas-Uele: service use at HGR Ganga fell from 29.5% in June to 20.3% in September 2026 against a 60% norm. Haut-Uele: an assessment of CH Bolebole (Wamba) found low service use through fear of contamination, missed routine vaccination and chronic-disease appointments, insufficient latrines and showers and a 55% tracer-medicine stock-out.

Ituri psychosocial coverage reaches 14 of 28 affected zones (50.0%) and 12 of the 42 latest confirmed cases (28.6%) are not yet supported; deployment of the psychologists and psychosocial workers trained in Mandima is awaited; Bas-Uele's support for its 3 confirmed cases is delayed, Tshopo's Wanie-Rukula workers remain to be trained and Haut-Uele lacks IT equipment, motorbikes and nutrition kits.

Ituri community engagement reporting completeness is low (9 of 28 zones, 32.1%) and the single Komanda incident is unresolved; Nord-Kivu received 191 of 650 expected community alerts (29.4%), resolved 2 of 5 incidents (40.0%) and engaged 1718 of 4750 people (36.2%); in Haut-Uele two reported incidents (a body taken from a health centre and the death of a confirmed patient who had left isolation) are still being handled.

Tshopo: attacks and threats against response teams are reported and confirmed case number 53 is still in the community; Haut-Uele: a family removed a body from a health centre after refusing a swab, and a confirmed patient who had left isolation in Isiro died in the Bala health area (Rungu); Ituri: the Avakubi PoC remains non-functional for insecurity and reluctance persists at Mongbwalu, Fataki and Komanda.

priorities: Strengthen epidemiological surveillance and contact follow-up to limit community transmission: contact follow-up rose from 76.9% to 77.8% but stays below the 95% threshold, Bunia is critical at 38.8%, and 23 suspects remain uninvestigated (20 Nord-Kivu, 3 Ituri).

The prose says seven provinces transmitted and prints counts for six (Sud-Ubangi, Nord-Ubangi, Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, Nord-Kivu), each matching its printed rate. Ituri prints no count or rate; the national less the six rows leaves 5822/8663, which is a remainder by difference and is not promoted. The key messages print Bunia at 38.8% (SR157: 26.0%) with no counts.

Nord-Kivu (page 7): 509 hospitalized (58 children under five), 3 critical; global CTE/CT occupancy printed 81.0% (332/410), suspects 166/192 (86.5%) and confirmed 166/218 (76.1%); 177 patients (34.8%) in facilities that are not CTE/CT. 332+177=509 reconciles. The 81.0% is a CTE/CT-only rate and the census exceeds the bed count, so no all-census occupancy is inferred. Data completeness 86% (Kyondo and Vuhovi missing). Hot meals went to 129 confirmed and 172 suspects, which do not match the 166/166 split; not used.
Nord-Kivu stock flow: SR157's printed 450 plus 154 admissions minus 95 exits gives 509, the printed census.

Ituri care (page 7): 431 patients follows exactly from SR157's 429 plus 83 admissions minus 81 exits and splits 193 confirmed and 238 suspects; the printed 42.5% has no bed denominator and none is derived. Hot meals reached 411 of 420 patients (97.9%), a base that differs from the 431 census. 34 patients were moved by ambulance and 27 blood bags went to 4 CTE. 75 children received nutritional care (11 CTE, 4 creche, 60 community).

Tshopo care (page 7): SR157's 16 plus 3 suspect admissions minus 2 recovered exits gives 17, against the printed 13 (13/36 is the printed 36.1%). Tableau 2 prints 2 new Tshopo confirmations (Kabondo, Tshopo) while all 3 admissions are suspects. The challenge names 4 confirmed cases from Bafwasende lost to follow-up (SR157: 6 of 7 lost patients were confirmed cases from Bafwasende). Not repaired.

Haut-Uele and Bas-Uele care (page 7): both print panels again after none in SR157. Haut-Uele prints 29 patients (9 confirmed, 20 suspects) for 169 beds (17.2%) after 4 admissions and 28 exits (7 recovered at Pawa, 1 escape, 1 transfer to the HGR). Bas-Uele prints 47 patients after 20 admissions and no exit, with its 3 confirmed beds full (100.0%); its challenge separately counts 44 suspects isolated in health facilities. Isolation: the cover 1029 equals the five printed provincial stocks 431+509+13+47+29 exactly; no residual. No national confirmed/suspect split is printed or derived.

Laboratory (page 6): 514 samples, 85 positive (16.5%), split 56 living and 29 deceased; deceased positives match Tableau 2's community deaths in every province and every printed provincial positivity matches its counts. Nord-Ubangi's 1 positive of 4 (25%) is printed as '1 vant' and read as living, consistent with Tableau 2 printing no Nord-Ubangi death. Bas-Uele's 2 samples were negative.
Key messages (page 10) agree with Tableau 3 and the prose on 533/556 investigated (95.9%) and 23 uninvestigated (20 Nord-Kivu, 3 Ituri), and on contact follow-up rising from 76.9% to 77.8%.

Vaccination (page 8): Ituri frontline-worker vaccination and the efficacy research are paused pending research committee validation; the cumulative stays at 1260. Nord-Kivu vaccinated 150 frontline workers in Beni, bringing the cumulative to 472 of 7105 (6.6%) (SR157's 322 plus 150), with 128 of 600 doses left and 1 non-serious adverse event; its challenge restates 6.6% against a provincial target of 36070 in 15 zones, a different base. Haut-Uele's frontline campaign ended at 589 (470 Isiro, 80 Pawa, 39 Wamba). Bas-Uele keeps 11.4% (1500/13202). No efficacy signal against BDBV is inferred.

SMSPS (page 9): Ituri prints 30 of 42 confirmed cases supported and its challenge 12 of the 42 latest confirmed cases not yet supported; Nord-Kivu prints 30 of 48 new cases. 42 and 48 are SR157's Ituri and Nord-Kivu daily counts, not SR158's 43 and 33. Not repaired.

IPC (page 7): Ituri prints 85 EDS done of 115 alerts (6 deferred) while its challenge prints 21 EDS failed (115 - 85 = 30); Nord-Kivu prints 48 EDS done for 53 alerts plus 40 deferred from the day before while its challenge prints 44 deferred (53 + 40 - 48 = 45). Both preserved.

CREC (page 9): the paragraph headed 'Au Nord Ubangi' runs on into figures for Isiro, Wamba, Libiki and Rungu, which are in Haut-Uele; the Haut-Uele heading appears to be missing ('Communautaires39 visites'). Read as a heading merge, not repaired.

Security and care (pages 7 and 10): Haut-Uele reports an escape among its 28 exits and, under security, that a confirmed patient who had left isolation in Isiro died in the Bala health area (Rungu); Tableau 2 prints no death for Isiro or Rungu this edition (Haut-Uele's 3 deaths are at Pawa). Not reconciled.
